issues.legal_issue: Compensation for a large acquired area containing land with different locations and characteristics must be determined by reasonable classification rather than by applying one uniform rate.
material_facts: The acquisition covered a large area containing lands abutting a national highway bypass and lands in the interior.
The land had been classified into different categories, and the court found that location and land category affected market value.
The High Court had applied a uniform rate to all the lands.
The Court considered the sale evidence unreliable in part, including a deed it described as fake.
issues.conclusion: The uniform rate was based on an incorrect principle. The lands had to be classified by location and category: land within about 500 yards of the main road was to receive the higher rate regardless of soil quality, while other lands were to receive rates according to their category.
issues.legal_principle: Market value is assessed by considering whether a willing and prudent purchaser would buy the land, with its existing features, at the proposed value. Although valuation involves some guesswork, it must have a reasonable basis and avoid imagination. Where a large acquisition includes land abutting a main road and land in the interior, reasonable demarcation or classification is necessary because the lands do not have uniform market value.

rule.if: compensation_valuation_appeal and large_acquired_area and land_varies_by_road_access and land_varies_by_category

predicates.compensation_valuation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the valuation of acquired land.
predicates.large_acquired_area: The acquisition covers a large area of land.
predicates.land_varies_by_road_access: Some acquired land is near a main road while other acquired land is in the interior.
predicates.land_varies_by_category: The acquired land differs in category or other characteristics relevant to its market value.

issues.definition: When a valuation appeal concerns a large acquisition containing land that differs in road access and category, compensation is determined by classifying land according to location and category.

issues.legal_issue: The constitutional guarantee of equality does not require a uniform compensation rate for acquired lands that differ in characteristics and market value.
material_facts: The claimants argued that different rates for different land classes were arbitrary and violated equality.
The acquired lands differed in location and other characteristics, and the Court found that they would not command the same market value in an open-market sale.
issues.conclusion: The equality guarantee did not require the same compensation rate for all the acquired lands, and classification with different rates was not invalid on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the equality guarantee does not apply to require identical compensation where lands are not equal in all relevant respects and would not command the same market value when sold by a willing vendor to a willing purchaser.

predicates.compensation_determination_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the amount of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.lands_differ_in_relevant_characteristics: The acquired lands differ in characteristics relevant to their value.
predicates.lands_have_different_market_values: The lands would not command the same market value in an open-market sale.

issues.definition: In a compensation proceeding, differing rates are permissible when the acquired lands differ in relevant characteristics and market value.

issues.legal_issue: Claimants whose compensation is enhanced are entitled to the applicable statutory additions to that enhanced compensation.
material_facts: The Court modified the compensation awards and enhanced compensation for the claimants.
The Court specified that the claimants were entitled to solatium, interest, and an additional annual amount on the enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to solatium, interest, and the additional amount under section 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, on the enhanced compensation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for the additional amount, and directed payment of solatium and interest on the enhanced compensation.

predicates.compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.compensation_is_enhanced: The compensation payable to the claimants is increased.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal results in increased compensation, the claimants receive the statutory additions on that increased compensation.

issues.legal_issue: An interested person who did not seek a reference may obtain re-determination of compensation on the basis of a court award if the land was covered by the same acquisition notification and the application is filed within the prescribed period.
material_facts: Some interested persons had not sought a reference under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Their land was covered by the same notification as land for which a reference court enhanced compensation.
An application for re-determination was filed within three months of the reference court's award, applying the statutory computation rules.
issues.conclusion: The timely applicant was entitled to re-determination of compensation on the basis of the compensation awarded by the reference court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28-A(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, permits interested persons who did not seek a section 18 reference, but whose land was covered by the same section 4(1) notification, to apply to the Collector for re-determination on the basis of the court award. Under the proviso, the day the award was pronounced and the time required to obtain a copy are excluded when computing the three-month period.

rule.if: compensation_redetermination_proceeding and interested_owner_did_not_seek_reference and land_shared_acquisition_notification and application_within_computed_limit

predicates.compensation_redetermination_proceeding: The proceeding seeks re-determination of compensation by the acquiring authority on the basis of a court award.
predicates.interested_owner_did_not_seek_reference: The interested person did not seek a reference against the original compensation award.
predicates.land_shared_acquisition_notification: The person's land was covered by the same acquisition notification as land considered in the court award.
predicates.application_within_computed_limit: The person filed the written application within the applicable time limit, computed after excluding the specified time for the award and obtaining its copy.

issues.definition: An interested person who did not seek a reference is entitled to court-award-based re-determination when the land shared the acquisition notification and the application was timely.

issues.legal_issue: An application for re-determination of compensation filed after the prescribed period is barred.
material_facts: Interested persons applied for re-determination on the basis of reference-court awards.
The applications were filed more than three months after the relevant awards, after accounting for the time excluded under the statutory computation rule.
The Collector nevertheless granted enhanced compensation on some applications.
issues.conclusion: The late applications were barred, and compensation granted on their basis was illegal; the challenged orders granting that compensation were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28-A(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, requires a written application within three months of the reference court's award. The proviso excludes the day the award was pronounced and the time required to obtain a copy; an application outside the resulting period is barred.

predicates.compensation_redetermination_proceeding: The proceeding seeks re-determination of compensation by the acquiring authority on the basis of a court award.
predicates.interested_owner_did_not_seek_reference: The interested person did not seek a reference against the original compensation award.
predicates.application_outside_computed_limit: The person filed the written application after the applicable time limit, computed after excluding the specified time for the award and obtaining its copy.

issues.definition: A person who did not seek a reference cannot obtain re-determination through an application filed after the applicable computed time limit.

issues.legal_issue: A cross-appeal seeking further enhancement of compensation is dismissed when the principal appeal succeeds in setting aside or modifying the enhancement challenged in that appeal.
material_facts: The cross-appeals sought further enhancement of compensation granted by the High Court.
The Union's appeals against the compensation awards were allowed.
issues.conclusion: The cross-appeals seeking further enhancement were dismissed because the Union's appeals had been allowed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court dismissed the cross-appeals for further enhancement in light of its decision allowing the principal appeals; it relied on no separate legal authority for this disposition.

predicates.cross_appeal_seeking_further_compensatio: The proceeding is a cross-appeal seeking further enhancement of compensation.
predicates.principal_appeal_against_enhancement_is_: The principal appeal challenging the compensation enhancement is allowed.

issues.definition: A cross-appeal seeking further compensation is dismissed when the principal appeal against the enhancement is allowed.
